column11: all of it, for what this unit can be priced on. Ubrelvy is indicated 'for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults' (DailyMed set id fd9f9458-fd96-4688-be3f-f77b3d1af6ab, revised 2025-06-05). The dossier's own pending catalyst, NCT06417775, enrols 496 adults aged 18 and over with menstrual migraine (ClinicalTrials.gov, read 2026-10-27, condition 'Migraine'), and menstrual migraine is a timing of attacks within adult migraine rather than a different disease, so those patients are already inside the approved label and inside the $1,271mm the asset reports
column12: the two paediatric studies, NCT05125302 and NCT05127954 at ages 6 to 17, are a genuine age extension that the label excludes, and they are deliberately not priced: no US migraine prevalence for ages 6 to 17 on ICHD criteria could be sourced in this session. Searched Europe PMC for US paediatric and adolescent migraine prevalence, PubMed for the AMPP age bands, and the NHIS and NHANES summaries. What was found measures something else - frequent or severe headache in 6% of 5-17 year olds (Pawlowski C et al., Clin Pediatr 2019;58:1502-1508, PMID 31522542, NHIS 2007-2015, n=57,272) and 17.1% of 4-18 year olds (Lateef TM et al., J Child Neurol 2009;24:536-543, PMID 19406755, NHANES) - neither of which is migraine by ICHD criteria. Taking either as the migraine pool would overstate it and neither was taken. What would settle it: a US ICHD-criteria migraine prevalence for ages 6 to 17, which would make this a priced layer on the same shape as the Qulipta file's adolescent row. Note also that Qulipta's file prices the 12-17 band off the same 31,236,457 pool; because this unit prices no incremental population at all, the two cannot double count the same patient
